title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate the compromised environment, identify the persistence mechanisms, trace the C2 communication, and detect lateral movement to a secondary target.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The BRICKSTORM backdoor is a sophisticated 64-bit ELF executable written in Go, designed to evade detection through advanced techniques such as SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution. This backdoor has been observed using Domain Name System (DNS) over HTTPS (DoH), nested TLS encryption, and abusing legitimate cloud services to hide its activities. The malware exhibits command-and-control (C2) capabilities, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and persistence mechanisms.

Your task is to investigate the compromised environment, identify the persistence mechanisms, trace the C2 communication, and detect lateral movement to a secondary target.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious service running on the target host that is responsible for C2 communication
levels.content: Investigate the running services on the `target` host. Identify the service that is listening on port 443 and is responsible for C2 communication. The flag is the name of the service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using the systemctl command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to C2 communication.

levels.title: Identify the persistence mechanism used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor
levels.content: Examine the systemd services and timers on the `target` host. Identify the persistence mechanism that ensures the backdoor service runs continuously. The flag is the name of the timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers can be listed using the systemctl command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for timers that might be related to the backdoor's persistence.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd timers that run periodically.

levels.title: Detect the lateral movement mechanism used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor
levels.content: Investigate the network connections and services on the `target` host. Identify the mechanism used for lateral movement to the `next-target` host. The flag is the name of the service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using the systemctl command.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that might be transferring data to the `next-target` host.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for services that use rsync or SSH.
